newsitem.title: CHILE: Pinochet backtracks on Chile coup suggestion.
newsitem.headline: Pinochet backtracks on Chile coup suggestion.

text.p: Former military ruler Gen. Augusto Pinochet sought to play down on Wednesday his suggestion that Chile's armed forces might stage a coup like the one in 1973 that overthrew a socialist government.
Pinochet, 80, denied his remark was aimed at a popular socialist Cabinet minister expected to run for president in 1999 and said he would probably be dead by then anyway.

Pinochet implied on Tuesday that the armed forces might someday carry out a coup like that in September 1973 which overthrew Marxist president Salvador Allende and brought them to power for nearly 17 years.

"We arrived in the year 1973, when a socialist president had left. And take care -- we could do it again," Pinochet said in a jocular tone in a speech to rightist supporters in a Santiago social club.

Local news media took the statement to be a reference to Public Works Minister Ricardo Lagos, a socialist and opponent of Pinochet's during military rule who holds a wide lead in public opinion polls for the 1999 elections.
But Pinochet quashed that idea, saying, "I was never talking about Lagos, and anyway I'll be dead by then."
Lagos, who has been building bridges to the military and recently appeared in public with Pinochet, and other government officials moved swiftly to minimise the importance of Pinochet's remarks.
"I get the impression he was saying it in jest," Lagos told reporters. "He was speaking in a joking tone."
President Eduardo Frei, asked about the comments at a Latin American summit meeting in Bolivia, replied tersely: "Democracy is irreversible. All the presidents here agree on that."

The chief government spokesman would not comment, because "we are people who look to the future," and Interior Minister Carlos Figueroa dismissed it as the sort of statement military leaders often make in September, the anniversary of the 1973 coup.
"Unfortunately, September comes and expressions of all kinds crop up which, in my opinion, don't help to achieve the reconciliation to which we're all committed," Figueroa said.
Pinochet handed power over to an elected civilian president in March 1990 but remains commander in chief of the army and undisputed ideological leader of Chile's powerful armed forces.
